[Benzinga news, 2026-10-21T15:24:41Z, by Vandana Singh] Danaher Beats Profit Estimates, Raises Outlook as Customer Demand Improves
Danaher topped Q3 earnings estimates at $2.11 per share on $6.55 billion revenue, raising its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook on steady biopharma demand.
Danaher Corp. (NYSE: DHR ) on Wednesday reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share, beating the analyst consensus estimate of $1.92 . Revenue rose 8.5% year over year to $6.6 billion, beating the analysts’ expectations of $6.559 billion. Core Revenue Acceleration and Operating Margin Strength Core revenue rose 3% year over year, in line with management’s guidance of 2%-3%. Excluding respiratory testing revenue, core revenue increased 5.5% . Julie Sawyer Montgomery , President and CEO, stated, “We delivered better-than-expected third-quarter revenue, earnings and cash flow, and are encouraged by the improving trends we saw across our end markets.” “The continued acceleration in core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue , together with DBS-driven execution, drove double-digit adjusted EPS growth and underscored our ability to convert improving demand into strong financial performance,” Montgomery further commented. The company delivered an adjusted operating profit margin of nearly 30%. Read Also: Danaher Brings NVIDIA AI Into Scientific Instruments in Push for Faster Discoveries End-Market Dynamics Montgomery said in an earnings call , “We’re particularly encouraged by the improved momentum we saw across our businesses. Underlying demand across large pharma and biopharma remained robust, biotech activity continued to strengthen, and while academic demand remained below historic levels, demand improved sequentially.” She added clinical and applied end markets remained healthy and continued to perform well. Danaher CFO Matt Gugino said healthier funding and investment levels supported Biotechnology and life sciences, and diagnostics continued to move beyond the most significant impacts of China’s healthcare policy changes. Raised Fiscal 2026 Guidance For the fourth quarter of 2026 , Danaher anticipates that non-GAAP core revenue excluding respiratory revenue will increase in the 4.0% to 5.0% range year-over-year. The company expects respiratory revenue to be an approximately 150 basis point headwind, resulting in core revenue growth of approximately 3.0%. Danaher raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings forecast from $8.45-$8.60 per share to $8.57-$8.62 per share versus the consensus of $8.51. Early Fiscal 2027 Perspective During the earnings call, CFO Gugino provided an early perspective on the fiscal 2027 outlook. “We’re encouraged by the improvement in the end markets and the growth we’ve delivered throughout 2026. Excluding respiratory revenue, core revenue growth has averaged 4% to 5% over the past several quarters. So as we look to 2027, we think that 4% to 5% core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue is the right starting point as we sit today.” DHR Stock Price Activity: Danaher shares are trading higher by 3.08% at $231.15 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data . [Benzinga news, 2026-10-21T14:14:55Z, by Vandana Singh] GSK Wins FDA Approval For Chronic Hepatitis B Drug
FDA clears GSK Hibsago for chronic hepatitis B in adults, delivering strong functional cure rates and suppressing viral replication targets.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday approved GSK plc’s (NYSE: GSK ) Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection to treat adult chronic hepatitis B patients without cirrhosis. FDA Clears First-In-Class Treatment Under FDA priority review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, regulators cleared the weekly subcutaneous injection for adults who have received antiviral therapy for at least six months, maintain suppressed viral DNA, and exhibit surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less. The agency also cleared the Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a companion diagnostic to select and monitor patients. Chronic hepatitis B causes long-term liver infection, which increases the risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer. As a first-in-class antisense oligonucleotide, Hibsago disables the genetic instructions that the hepatitis B virus uses to replicate and generate viral proteins, decreasing circulating virus and antigen levels. Read Also: FDA Clears GSK Drug That Could Change How Certain Rectal Cancers Are Treated Phase 3 Trials Show Significant Cure Rates The approval is based on data from the B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 phase 3 trials. Across these studies, a 24-week Hibsago regimen alongside existing antiviral medicine enabled 24% of participants to stop baseline medication, compared to zero in the placebo group. Twenty-four weeks after halting all therapies, 19% of Hibsago patients (233 of 1,220) sustained a functional cure, meaning viral DNA and HBsAg remained undetectable. In contrast, placebo achieved zero responses, while standard care alone typically achieves less than 1% after one year. Among participants with baseline antigen levels at or below 1,000 IU/mL—a group representing about 45% of global cases—functional cure rates reached 26% (200 of 768). Exploratory data at week 72 showed 49% of overall participants reduced surface antigen levels to 100 IU/mL or less. Safety Profile And Boxed Warnings Hibsago carries a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts that increase bleeding risks. Regulators also warned of kidney decline, inflammatory reactions like vasculitis, and improper administration risks. [Benzinga news, 2026-10-21T13:31:59Z, by staff] Analog Devices Issues Statement Regarding Tutanota Mini-Tender Offer
Analog Devices, Inc. has requested that its shareholders be provided with a copy of its official response regarding a mini-tender offer initiated by Tutanota for shares of ADI common stock.
Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI) has issued a formal communication regarding a mini-tender offer for its common stock initiated by Tutanota. The company has requested that this response be included with all materials distributed to shareholders concerning the offer. This action is a standard governance procedure to ensure shareholders are informed of the company's position on the unsolicited tender offer.
